name: Damn Vulnerable NodeJS Application (DVNA)
intendedUse: Describes itself as a simple Node.js application to demonstrate the OWASP Top 10 and teach fixing them (README).

source.note: No tags. Application code is unchanged since 2018-08-28; later commits touch docs and README only, so the source matches the 2018-10-08 image.

image.note: Built 2018-10-08; amd64 only (runs under emulation on arm64). Uses SQLite, so no database container is needed.

builtBy: Claude (AI-assisted) from the solution guide at the pinned commit; to be checked by labeller A before registration.

auth.note: All /app routes except /app/redirect need a session. The runner registers a throwaway local user through /register and logs in through /login.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection
vulnerabilities.description: User search concatenates the login field into a raw SQL query.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection
vulnerabilities.description: Ping tool passes the address field to a shell command.

vulnerabilities.title: Command Injection (source)
vulnerabilities.description: child_process exec with the request body concatenated into the command.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Reset Password
vulnerabilities.description: Reset token is the MD5 of the username.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Session Secret
vulnerabilities.description: Session signing secret is a well-known example string hardcoded in server.js.

vulnerabilities.title: Hashed Passwords Disclosed
vulnerabilities.description: Admin users API returns whole user objects, password hashes included.
vulnerabilities.note: Judging this needs knowing which fields a user may see.

vulnerabilities.title: Logging of sensitive information
vulnerabilities.description: SQL queries with credentials are logged.

vulnerabilities.title: XML External Entities
vulnerabilities.description: Bulk product import parses XML with external entities enabled.

vulnerabilities.title: Unauthorized Access to Users API
vulnerabilities.description: Any logged-in user can call the admin users API.

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authorization check in Edit User
vulnerabilities.description: Edit user accepts another user id from the form.

vulnerabilities.title: Application sends Stack Trace
vulnerabilities.description: Calculator returns a stack trace on malformed input.
vulnerabilities.note: Needs a malformed request body, so it counts only in runs that send crafted input.

vulnerabilities.title: X-Powered-By header
vulnerabilities.description: Express sends X-Powered-By on every response.

vulnerabilities.title: Reflected XSS in Search Query
vulnerabilities.description: Product search echoes the query unescaped into the page.

vulnerabilities.title: Stored XSS in Product Listing
vulnerabilities.description: Product fields are rendered unescaped.

vulnerabilities.title: DOM XSS in user listing
vulnerabilities.description: Admin user list writes API data with innerHTML.
vulnerabilities.note: The source-visible sink is scored separately as dom-xss-users-source.

vulnerabilities.title: DOM XSS in user listing (source)
vulnerabilities.description: innerHTML assignment of API data in an EJS template script block.
vulnerabilities.note: The sink is in an .ejs template, not a .js file.

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Deserialization
vulnerabilities.description: Legacy bulk import unserializes uploaded data with node-serialize.

vulnerabilities.title: mathjs Remote Code Execution
vulnerabilities.description: Outdated mathjs evaluates user input; the library version has an RCE advisory.
vulnerabilities.note: Server-side npm dependency; url+repo mode does not match npm advisories.

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficient Logging and Monitoring
vulnerabilities.description: Failed logins are not logged.

vulnerabilities.title: CSRF in Add/Edit product, User Edit
vulnerabilities.description: State-changing forms have no CSRF token.

vulnerabilities.title: Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards
vulnerabilities.description: The redirect route sends the user to any url parameter.
